records.name: Dyngjusandur
records.sand_source_verbatim: Primary source is Dyngjujökull (outlet glacier). In summer, ablation of the glacier feeds a number of outlet streams. Due to percolation, downstream transmission losses occur and results in the accumulation of sand available for aeolian transport at the
records.sand_characteristics_verbatim: Dominated by glass grains (80-90%). Remaining fractions corresponds to a few percent of olivine, pyroxene, and plagioclase. Overall, glass grains comprise ~80% of sand and crystalline phases ~20% (a).
records.references_verbatim: a: Baratoux et al. (2011) Volcanic sands of Iceland: Diverse origins of aeolian sand deposits revealed at Dyngjusandur and Lambahraun. Earth Surface Processes and Landforms, v. 36, no. 13, pg. 1789-1808.
